speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand your condition better, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you recall any recent trauma to your wrist?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Erythema Migrans and Lyme Arthritis). The patient is a 17-year-old male from Minnesota with a 3-day history of worsening left wrist pain, chills, malaise, and a history of self-resolving knee pain. The travel history and joint symptoms are highly suggestive of disseminated Lyme disease. I am proceeding with this diagnosis based on the clinical presentation and epidemiology. No further testing is required at this moment.
